To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the textbook series is not culturally appropriate to the needs of Mongol students in Inner Mongolia.

the textbook series is unbalanced in its representations of cultures of the three circles, and it also lacks diversity in its representations of race, ethnicity, gender/sex, social class, people with disabilities.
EFL textbooks for Inner Mongolian ethnic students in China represent multiculturalism in an unbalanced and stereotypical way, which is not beneficial to students' multicultural awareness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways that the EFL textbooks represent the world in a particular way, which reflects and perpetuates the unequal power relations among countries and multicultural variables.
the cultural contents of EFL textbooks in Inner Mongolia and how they can be used to promote a multicultural perspective.
the ways in which EFL textbooks can be a site for the production and dissemination of power relations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the textbook is not a neutral tool, but rather an ideological instrument that reflects and reproduces the dominant culture and power relations.

the textbook series under investigation does not provide the students with an adequate representation of multiculturalism and power relations, which are essential to EFL education in the Inner circle.
the cultural representations in the textbook series are unbalanced, stereotypically and lack diversity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the current textbook series for EFL education among ethnic Mongols in Inner Mongolia is not multicultural enough and needs to include a wider range of countries, races/ethnicities, social classes and gender/sexualities.
the current textbooks for EFL education among ethnic Mongols lack a critical multicultural perspective and are therefore not appropriate for the current multicultural context in China.
we need a critical multicultural perspective to better understand the power relations that are embedded in EFL textbooks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cultural contents in EFL textbooks for Mongol students should be more diverse, inclusive, and critical.

a critical multiculturalism perspective can help students, educators, and textbook writers better understand and address the issues of cultural representations and power relations in EFL textbooks, which can lead to more equitable and inclusive learning environments.
the EFL textbook is an important site for the construction of cultural knowledge.
